editorial:
Imagine you are just trying to get to a car show, but suddenly every single vehicle on the road is trying to kill you. That is the wild ride you get with Harlan Hollis, a filmmaker who finds himself hunted by a group of professional killers. The whole vibe is like a giant, chaotic game of cat and mouse played out on the highway. It mixes a bit of mystery with a lot of explosions, making it feel like a comic book brought to life. You will spend most of the time wondering why these people want him dead and how he is going to survive the madness.

What really pops here are the stunts. Since the director loves cars, the crashes are real and look amazing. The acting is a bit over-the-top, but that actually fits the silly tone of the film. While the plot can be a bit thin in some spots, the non-stop action keeps you from getting bored.
endingExplained: You find out that the killers were hired because Harlan possesses a secret that some powerful people want to keep hidden. After a massive final showdown involving huge crashes and fire, Harlan manages to outsmart his pursuers. The bad guys end up destroyed in their own traps, and the mystery of who paid for the hits is finally solved. He survives the ordeal, proving that his driving skills are just as good as his filmmaking.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves 80s action movies and big car crashes.
